args.text: When the description states that an implementation can take one of several alternative forms, model the alternatives as separate tasks on mutually exclusive branches, using an exclusive gateway to select a branch and to merge the branches before the next common activity.

trace.reason: Check whether documented guidance already covers modeling explicitly stated implementation alternatives and the related exclusive gateways.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use an inclusive split when one or more conditions can be true; use an inclusive join to synchronize only activated reachable branches.
Use an exclusive merge for alternative paths; it does not wait for inactive alternatives.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.

args.text: When a description lists mutually exclusive ways to implement a solution, model each way as a separate task on an exclusive branch, then merge the branches before the next common activity.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already captures modeling explicitly stated alternative implementation options.

result.rule: When the description says an activity may take place before a later activity: Model the optional activity as a decision branch with a path that bypasses it; merge the paths before the later activity.

When When a description names multiple distinct activities within one phase and states that the process continues only after every activity is finished,: model the activities as parallel branches with a parallel split and join, rather than as a sequence.

When the description states that an item may be put away in one of multiple alternative locations: Model each alternative destination as a separate activity on a mutually exclusive branch, distinct from other stated handling activities.

When the description states that named activities may be performed as optional additions to the main sequence: Model each named activity in the optional flow, using gateways to reflect whether the activities are alternatives or whether one or more may occur.

args.text: When naming BPMN elements, use labels that faithfully represent the actions and outcomes stated in the process description; do not substitute a different action or add unsupported details.

trace.reason: Check whether an existing documented guideline already covers faithful BPMN labeling.

result.rule: Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
Create reusable bpmn:message elements and messageRef only when communication content or shared message identity matters.

Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.

result.rule: When the description states an activity and provides criteria or other supporting details that are not needed to identify that activity: Label the BPMN element with a concise name for the stated action; omit supporting details that do not distinguish it from another modeled activity, while preserving details that are themselves distinct actions or alternatives.

When the description names a specific activity and distinguishes it from a related preceding or subsequent activity: Label the BPMN activity with the action stated in the description; do not substitute a related action that the description treats as separate or does not state.
When the description explicitly states the object or scope of an activity: Retain that meaningful object or scope in the BPMN task label while keeping the label concise.
When the description explicitly states the outcome that terminates the process: Label the end event to reflect that stated outcome; do not use an unstated or different outcome.
